summary: Refused and escalated. The request asks this agent to approve a candidate definition for GL-101 and mark it as an official Critical Data Element. Approving a definition and setting CDE status are human Data Steward decisions; this agent has zero decision authority and no write capability. No candidate definition text was supplied in the request, so there is nothing to approve or compare. For context only: the synthetic glossary holds GL-101 'Settlement Date' (status Approved, v1.0, owner recorded as Avery Example (SYNTHETIC), recorded_cde_flag true), and a possible_duplicate link to GL-204, a second 'Settlement Date' entry with a different definition and no CDE flag. The existing recorded CDE flag on GL-101 is a recorded value only; no CDE-criteria policy document has been identified, so it cannot be validated here.
conflicts_identified: GL-101 and GL-204 both define 'Settlement Date' with different wording. GL-101: 'The date on which cash and securities are exchanged to complete a trade.' (actual exchange). GL-204: 'The contractual date by which payment and delivery of a trade must complete, as agreed at execution.' (contractual due date). A term link marks them as possible_duplicate. The two may mean different things (actual vs contractual date). Both are surfaced; neither is picked.
CDE flag inconsistency across the two entries: GL-101 has recorded_cde_flag true; GL-204, a second entry for the same term name, has recorded_cde_flag false.
